articles.title: Ireland men set for maiden tour of Pakistan in January, to play three ODIs
articles.summary:
The Ireland men’s team will tour Pakistan in January for the first time to play three One-day Internationals against the hosts, the cricket boards of both countries announced on Thursday.

The visitors, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), are scheduled to arrive in the country on Jan 9, and will take on national developmental side Pakistan Shaheens for three warm-up one-day matches between Jan 13 and 17.

The ODIs are set for Jan 20, 22 and 24. All six matches, the PCB said, will be played at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium.

The series was originally planned to be a multi-format one before plans were changed with the proximity of the 2027 World Cup in mind.

“While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027,” Graeme West, Director of High Performance at Cricket Ireland, said in a statement.

This tour, therefore, is an important milestone for Ireland, who are also all set to feature in the upcoming World Cup Qualifier, through which they’ll try to secure their spot for next year’s showpiece.

“Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope,” West added.

For the hosts, meanwhile, the tour would be an opportunity to test their depth – especially through the Shaheens matches – and continue the fine-tuning process of their combinations ahead of the World Cup.

Pakistan made a statement of sorts about their ODI form, convincingly winning a tri-series, which featured England and Sri Lanka along with Shaheen Shah Afridi’s side.

Correction: An earlier version of this story stated that the Ireland team would be arriving next month. The error is regretted.

articles.title: SBCA chief removed as CM Murad orders sweeping action over building collapse in Karachi's Baloch Colony
articles.summary:
KARACHI: Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) director general, was removed from both the posts on Thursday on Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah’s directives following the collapse of an under-construction building in Karachi’s Baloch Colony the previous day.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

Regarding Shamshad, the CM further directed that his services be surrendered to the federal government. Moreover, a recommendation should be made to the federal government to suspend Shamshad and order a formal inquiry against him, the CM instructed.

Following CM Murad’s directives, the Sindh government notified Shamshad’s transfer.

The Services, General Administration and Coordination Department’s notification, seen by Dawn, said the BS-21 officer had been transferred “with immediate effect” and directed to report to the same department.

Meanwhile, the chairperson of the Inspection, Enquiries and Implementation Team Department, Bilal Memon, was posted as the Sindh local government secretary with immediate effect and until further orders, another notification by the Services, General Administration and Coordination Department said.

Apart from the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

He further directed that a “comprehensive and transparent” probe be carried out and strict action be taken against any other SBCA employee found responsible.

The statement quoted him as saying that any negligence resulting in the loss of lives or causing suffering to people would not be tolerated.

He said public safety must remain the “foremost responsibility” of every government department and warned that negligence in enforcing building regulations would lead to strict action, the statement added.

Sindh Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hasan Lanjar, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah, Karachi Commissioner Hassan Naqvi and other senior officials attended the meeting.

Separately, CM Murad said during a press conference in Karachi that authorities had halted the construction of 123 buildings that were being built under stay orders.

At least 123 buildings in this city were being constructed under stay orders,” he reiterated.

He added that he had asked the provincial law minister to speak to the chief justice and the court had been requested to decide the cases of those 123 buildings in 15 days.

He said the building that collapsed in Baloch Colony was also being constructed under a stay order.

The chief minister said that the government had identified 16 to 17 SBCA officers and ordered their suspension over misconduct. He added that he had further instructed that a legal case be filed against those officials so that they could be terminated under law and an example could be set.

CM Murad said that he had also ordered the removal of the SBCA chief. He stated that the government had requested the federal government to suspend him.

“We are going to have a reset in the Sindh Building Control Authority,” he announced.

Death toll rises to 4

On Wednesday, a ground-plus-five-storey building with one penthouse, covering 600 square yards, collapsed in Karachi’s Baloch Colony — at a time when over 20 workers were reported to be present at the site.

Officials and witnesses said that the building collapsed when work to dig a borehole was under way. On the day of the collapse, authorities had confirmed three deaths and injuries to 14 others.

The search operation, which was halted on Wednesday night, was resumed on Thursday, and search teams had pulled out another body by evening.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaanul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that the deceased was a middle-aged man, and the death toll had risen to four following the recovery of his body.

The body was recovered hours after Khan told Dawn in the afternoon that an information desk had been set up in collaboration with the East district administration and the families of 17 missing individuals had approached it.

According to Khan, the rescue authorities were taking extra care in the removal of the heavy debris from the area to find possible survivors. He said they had persuaded a private house owner to demolish the wall of his house to get another point of access to the collapsed building. Rescue workers also needed to enter the collapsed building, using sensors and vibration to find bodies before initiating debris removal operations.

Khan said the operation was a delicate one and the rescue service was avoiding using heavy machinery to prevent the possible loss of human life in case they were still alive under the debris. Initially, he said, the debris was being removed with help of heavy machinery, before a rescue operation was launched to find possible survivors.

On Wednesday, the now-removed East DC told Dawn it had transpired during the initial probe that the SBCA had given the approval for constructing the ground-plus-one-storey building to its owner.

However, the owner allegedly violated the approved plan and constructed six storeys. When the SBCA tried to halt the construction, the owner approached the court and got an order against the SBCA, he said. But the SBCA did not take any action against him.

Relatives of the missing persons on Thursday afternoon protested against the alleged slow pace of the rescue operation, blocking Sharea Faisal near Baloch Colony Bridge.

According to them, despite a day passing, they had received no more news about their missing loved ones and the officials were not providing them with any clarity.

According to a traffic police statement, both tracks of the main artery were blocked near Baloch Colony Bridge. Traffic was diverted on alternative routes for over half an hour, after which the protesters dispersed peacefully.

Earlier, in a fit of anger and sorrow, the protesters broke security barriers and entered cordoned areas, where contingents of the police prevented them from moving further.

The relatives told the media that they were not satisfied with the rescue operation. They said instead of destroying the collapsed building material with shovels, heavy crane machinery should be used to save the missing people from the debris.

14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished

The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis.

He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse, and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings into their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings.

Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT) Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar also visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes.

Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr. Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police five-day physical remand of the suspects.

Additional reporting by Sumair Abdullah

articles.title: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says
articles.summary:
The Makkah pact nations will discuss the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen when officials from the mutual defence agreement meet in Islamabad on Thursday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told AFP.

Asif said the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting and it is very important”, confirming that defence and foreign ministers from the Gulf kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan would attend.

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the pact in August, with the three Muslim nations pledging to come to each other’s aid in the event of an attack.

Saudi Arabia has faced repeated barrages by the Houthis in Yemen, with the group targeting cities, oil facilities and shipping since fighting in Yemen’s civil war intensified in July.

“Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear,” Khawaja said on Wednesday, praising Riyadh’s handling of the conflict with the Houthis, who hold swathes of territory in Yemen, including its capital Sanaa.

He said the pact, which was formed during the expansion of the war in the Middle East following US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February, was still at a “nascent stage”.

“Initially, we need to have frequent meetings to steer what is being formulated, in a way that in the next couple of months we have everything in place so that we can move forward,” he added.

Khawaja declined to comment on how the pact would react to a direct attack by Iran on Saudi Arabia and identified Israel as a possible threat to other countries in the region.

“The possibility of some conflict, or aggression from the Israeli side exists, so we need to close our ranks, the countries of this region,” he said.

Pakistan brokered a June accord that led to a brief halt in fighting between the US and Iran and set a roadmap for further agreement on reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz and for negotiations on Tehran’s nuclear programme.

But the truce collapsed, with Washington and Tehran accusing each other of violating the agreement, prompting months of shuttle diplomacy to resuscitate the ceasefire, led principally by mediators Qatar and Pakistan.

Khawaja said Pakistan had played “a very, very constructive role” between Washington and Tehran, but the outcome of ongoing mediation was “still fragile” and peace was “not yet embedded in a way people were expecting”.

articles.title: Security breach case: IHC seeks replies from parties on Imaan, Hadi's appeals against their conviction
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday issued notices and sought replies from parties on appeals filed by lawyers Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha against their convictions in a security breach case.

An anti-terrorism court (ATC) sentenced the husband-wife duo to 10 years in prison each, besides imposing fines on them, on Oct 29 in the 2024 case pertaining to the removal of security barriers, disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.

Imaan and Hadi filed appeals in the IHC against their convictions on Nov 7. They also sought the suspension of their sentences and release on bail pending the outcome of their appeals.

A division bench comprising Justice Inam Ameen Minhas and Justice Ayaz Shaukat took up their appeals today and issued the notices to the parties through a written order.

The court also issued notices and sought responses from parties on separate applications filed by both appellants for the suspension of their sentences.

Advocates Riasat Ali Azad, Zainab Janjua and Asif Ali Tamboli represented Imaan and Hadi at the hearing today.

Jailed, sentenced, re-arrested

They have been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts.

On September 17, following months of litigation before the courts, the SC suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and Hadi were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

While they remain imprisoned, their trial in the security breach case was conducted in jail. They were indicted in the case on Oct 7, despite their objections that they had not received copies of case documents and had not been allowed to meet their lawyers.

On Oct 26, they had also approached the Supreme Court challenging the IHC’s refusal to stay their jail trial.

On Nov 11, the Supreme Court disposed of a petition filed by the couple as infructuous, observing that the matter had become infructuous following the conclusion of the trial and their conviction.

The Supreme Court directed the IHC to decide on the petition filed by the couple in the case.

articles.title: Bilawal terms PTI a ‘political reality’, calls for restoring its trust in the ‘system’
articles.summary:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place.

Bilawal, who is on a visit to Punjab for the past few days, made the remarks while speaking at the Multan Press Club. He has made stops in Multan, Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh so far.

Responding to a query about him calling former premier Imran Khan a “political prisoner”, Bilawal explained that he made the “controversial” statement in a polarised political environment, where those terming him a political prisoner could not be convinced otherwise and those declaring him a convict and corrupt could not be convinced otherwise.

Bilawal stressed that in his speech, not the press queries, he made an observation that was not about Imran, but rather about Pakistan’s political history wherein elected premiers often end up going to jail later on or come to power after being imprisoned.

“Whatever opinion you may hold about Khan sahib, even if you think he is not a political prisoner, there is no denying the fact that PTI is a political reality,” the PPP chairman stressed.

He emphasised that even if Imran was considered a “convicted felon or terrorist or whatever”, prisoners in a respectable society were entitled to their rights.

Bilawal said that although the PTI founder “tried to deny my family those rights”, he would not want to continue the cycle of “repeating the same mistakes” in vengeance.

“Khan sahib is a convict, he is in jail, but PTI is a political reality. Until PTI’s trust is restored in this system […] and they are able to play their role in the Parliament, the reset that is being discussed cannot take place in that manner,” he maintained.

The PPP chairman’s latest remarks come amid a growing debate over a “system reset” in the country. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units, arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

In a similar vein, the Bhutto scion on Monday had called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system.

During Thursday’s address, Bilawal reiterated his call to regain the opposition’s “lost trust” in the system and for the government to undertake confidence-building measures to convince it that institutions such as the Parliament, the Election Commission, the courts, and the accountability system could be trusted again.

At the same time, the PPP chairman highlighted a similar “lack of trust” in the opposition on the government’s part and urged the opposition to view its role as a responsibility rather than a choice.

“They should sit in our finance committee in the Parliament. When the government presents the budget, [they should give their] input,” he said, adding that the opposition’s role was essential to tackling unemployment, inflation and poverty.

“But they haven’t been doing it for quite some time. They come for the judiciary, but there is also a committee for the judiciary, they do not sit in that either. They are not present in all committees of the Parliament,” Bilawal pointed out.

He called on the opposition to review if they benefitted from their boycott of such parliamentary initiatives, urging that it take part in the recently proposed electoral reforms committee.

“Until there are free and fair elections, until our country, our nation, all provinces, and all parties have confidence in this electoral system, there will be no trust, and the governments formed or referendums held as a result of that electoral system will lack legitimacy and strength,” Bilawal asserted.

The PPP chairman reiterated his stance that any “reset or reboot of our system” should be democratic and political, with all political stakeholders, including the opposition, made part of the conversation.

“If we want to make the Parliament functional, then all decisions have to be made in the Parliament alone,” he said, adding that decisions taken “outside the Parliament” would leave the system incapable of overcoming challenges.

Bilawal regretted that ongoing discussions in the Parliament, the federal cabinet, seminars, or even television talk shows did not pay attention to the fundamental issues faced by the public.

“People are distressed about managing two square meals. They’re worried whether they should educate their children or arrange medicines for their elders,” Bilawal said.

Bilawal noted there was “restlessness and distress” among Pakistan’s youth, who faced unemployment and, even if employed, their salaries were spent on just commuting to and from work.

“In my opinion, if we truly want this system to serve the public, if we truly want our country, our Pakistan, to be capable of facing every problem, whether they are economic hardships or foreign difficulties, then we will have to take steps as soon as possible so we can establish unity, political stability, and restore trust in all institutions,” Bilawal stated.

‘Non-existent press freedom’

During his address, the PPP chairman also highlighted the importance of a free press, adding that he wanted to restore the “power” previously held by press clubs across the country.

“With your voice, your columns, you used to make and topple governments,” the Bhutto scion remarked.

“I don’t want to topple any government, nor do I want to form another one. But I believe your role is to hold up a mirror to those sitting in power,” he added.

Bilawal said he was not denying “mistakes” made by him over time, insisting that his party’s intention was not to weaken the press.

He referred to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), which was amended in January 2025 despite countrywide protests by journalists’ bodies.

He remarked that regardless of the PPP’s intention, the country had now arrived at a point where press freedom was non-existent.

The PPP chairman noted that if the media was given space only to regurgitate what those in power talked about among themselves, then issues related to economic crises and difficulties faced by the people at the grassroots level would not come to the forefront.

Bilawal also elaborated on his earlier remarks about the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments, insisting that an impression was being given as if he was backing away from them or criticising them.

In his Nov 17 remark, the PPP chairman, who had strongly advocated for the amendments at the time of their passage, had said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor bilateral agreement; it was passed with brute majority”.

He had also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation.

The next day, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution.

“It’s not black and white,” Bilawal said today, stressing that the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment were passed through mutual consensus.

He defended that the 26th Amendment was passed with as much consensus as could be developed, while the 27th

articles.title: Local holiday announced in Islamabad, Rawalpindi on Nov 27
articles.summary:
A local holiday has been declared in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) and Rawalpindi for Nov 27 (Friday).

A notification issued by the Islamabad deputy commissioner stated that Nov 27 “has been declared a local holiday within the revenue limits of ICT”.

It noted that all essential services would remain operational during the holiday, including the Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad, the Capital Development Authority, the ICT administration, Islamabad police, the Islamabad Electric Supply Company, the Sui Northern Gas Pipeline Limited and hospitals.

Separately, the Rawalpindi deputy commissioner shared a notification on X stating that a local holiday had been declared in the district for Nov 27. He said that all schools, colleges and offices would remain closed.

The notification said that all “emergency dealing departments/institutions/authorities shall remain operational”.

“Moreover, all annual and supplementary examinations shall be conducted as per the approved schedule in all education institutes of Rawalpindi district,” it said.

Both notifications did not provide a reason for the holiday.

Meanwhile, a notice of expected partial closure was issued for the Rawalpindi-Islamabad metro system from Nov 26-28, as a result of expected “VIP movement”.

The notice warned of a possible suspension of the line from Kashmir Highway to the Pak Secretariat stations and said the closure of the last four stops was also under consideration.

The metro service from Saddar to Faiz Ahmed Faiz would remain operational, it added.

articles.title: Meta battles political storm in India as Congress party sues, stages protests
articles.summary:
India’s main opposition party, the Indian National Congress, has sued Meta and the federal government, saying that an automated content-removal system is blocking political posts and images of ​opposition leader Rahul Gandhi ahead of state elections.

The filing takes a week-long Congress campaign against Meta from the streets to the courtroom, and highlights Prime Minister ‌Narendra Modi’s automated takedown mandate, under which the Facebook and Instagram parent has restricted more than 5.4 million posts in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025.

In a court filing dated Nov 25 in the Delhi High Court, seen by Reuters, Congress’s youth wing social media head Manu Jain said the rules have become “an instrument for the suppression of lawful political expression”.

The case leaves Meta’s operations ​in India, the company’s biggest market, caught between a government whose rules strip platforms of legal protection if they fail to comply, and an opposition demanding it ​push back.

Congress argues that Meta’s system is blocking posts that are not “exactly identical” copies of content previously ordered removed, including birthday greetings, tributes ⁠and a wedding invitation featuring Gandhi. Meta says it moderates content in India in accordance with the law.

Meta declined to comment. India’s IT and home ministries, which are named as co-respondents ​in the lawsuit, did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

Modi’s government has maintained that such laws are essential to prevent the proliferation of illegal and harmful content online in ​a market of over 1.1 billion internet users.

Congress is urging the court to strike down the mandate for automated takedowns and also order Meta to restore the posts, as well as disclose blocking criteria.

Hearings are expected to begin in the coming days.

‘Automated tools’ mandate

India amended its IT rules in February to require large platforms to use technical measures “including automated tools” to find and block any post “exactly identical” to content already removed ​under a court order or a written government notice. Before that, platforms were asked only to “endeavour” to use such tools.

To comply, Meta has been restricting “100 per cent identical copies of content, at ​scale and in country” under India’s amended IT rules, its transparency report shows. The company says it is still testing and refining the system given the “unprecedented nature of this effort”.

Meta says it is required ‌to automatically ⁠restrict content at scale in only a “limited” number of countries, which it says explains the higher volumes.

Congress says the automated system is catching far more than exact duplicates. It is blocking birthday greetings, tributes and even a wedding invitation because they carry the photograph or name of opposition leader Gandhi, while “no order, notice, reason or even a ‘legal request’ has been disclosed,” the petition said.

In one case cited in the petition, a Nov 8 birthday greeting from a youth wing leader to a colleague, showing the colleague standing beside Gandhi, was blocked the same day.

“We ​restricted access to this content through an automated ​system implemented pursuant to legal requirements,” ⁠the notice to the user read.

India is also one of seven markets, including Brazil and Hong Kong, where Meta does not tell users which government authority sought a restriction, citing “legal obligations and regulatory considerations”, its transparency report shows. Elsewhere, it does so in most cases.

Wider offensive by Congress

The automated takedown system “distorts the level playing field” needed for a free and fair election, especially as party workers rely on Meta’s ​platforms to reach voters ⁠ahead of state polls due early next year, the petition says.

Facebook and Instagram have 400m and 515m users respectively in India, according to research firm DataReportal.

Congress has put up large hoardings in several cities depicting Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg in the traditional uniform of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, the ideological parent of Modi’s party.

Congress’s youth wing has protested near Meta offices and clashed with ⁠police in ​several cities in recent days. The BJP has accused the protesters of vandalising the offices of private companies.

At ​a closed-door meeting this week reported by Reuters, Congress told Meta to push back against first-instance takedown orders, as Elon Musk’s X has done, a source told Reuters. X is currently engaged in a legal battle against the government over ​its content-removal system.

Meta told Congress at the meeting that it was neutral towards all political parties and bound by local laws.

articles.title: Other realms
articles.summary:
IT was a moment of pride for Pakistan when PAF officer Muhammad Zeeshan Ali blasted off into space yesterday morning alongside his Chinese colleagues, astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi. As the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft entered orbit soon after lift-off, Wing Commander Ali became Pakistan’s first orbital astronaut, carrying with him “the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis”.

Three-and-a-half hours later, the Shenzhou-24 capsule docked with China’s Tiangong space station, where the crew from an earlier mission warmly greeted the arriving astronauts — especially their first foreign guest. Wing Commander Ali, who has been designated a payload specialist, will spend about a week in space working on four experiments covering radiation protection, space food security, oxygen-producing microorganisms, and self-healing carbon fibres.

With the successful launch of Shenzhou-24, Pakistan joins the ranks of around 50 countries that have sent their citizens into orbit. For years, China and Pakistan have worked closely in several sectors, ranging from defence and security to energy and infrastructure development under CPEC. As 2026 marks 75 years of Pakistan-China diplomatic relations, it is only fitting that spaceflights should be the next sphere of cooperation.

However, while a significant beginning has been made, it will be years before Pakistan can take the same strides in space technology as China. This moment of celebration must therefore give way to something more permanent — economic stability, greater investment in R&D, international collaborations in science and technology, and above all, a sound STEM education base.

With a large youth population comes a strong talent pool. But governments here have left it untapped. Instead, they have given free rein to illiteracy, poverty, and poor schooling, closing many doors to opportunity. Contrast this reality with a space flight by one man from the same country that has brought hope to millions — a fleeting triumph that could acquire permanence if the state prioritised people’s welfare.

“To every child who is watching while I am in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams,” was Zeeshan Ali’s message to youngsters as he set out to explore realms beyond Earth. Pakistan should not allow its children’s dreams to fade away.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: Govt to limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Thursday announced that it would limit additional fuel cost charges to consumers at 83 paise per unit (kWh) through a forward-looking adjustment on a quarterly basis, instead of Rs2.88 per unit in additional fuel cost it was seeking for December billing.

The Power Division, in a statement, said it has “proposed a Forward-looking Fuel Cost Adjustment (FFCA) mechanism wherein the increase … would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026” over the September FCA.

The statement came while the public hearing was in progress at the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) for an additional FCA of Rs2.88 per unit for electricity consumed in September and its billing in December.

The petition for higher FCA was filed by the Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) of the Power Division for all distribution companies (Discos), including K-Electric.

During the public hearing, the Power Division Additional Secretary Mehfooz Bhatti said the government as well as the consumers were facing increasing price shocks due to volatility in fuel supplies, particularly in the winters when cheaper hydropower generation dropped substantially.

He said the government had been working hard since the war-related challenges emerged to manage additional FCA shocks within Rs2 to 2.5 per unit through the provision of scarce and expensive imports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) at local gas rates and other efforts.

“We are bringing up a tariff band that provides pricing predictability as always demanded by the industry”, he said, adding that a policy directive had been secured from the government’s appropriate forums.

“The policy guidelines under section 31(4) of the Nepra law would be placed before you latest by tomorrow (Friday) morning. The government has cleared the policy directive covering the October-December period.”

Bhatti requested the Nepra to call an early public hearing if it was necessary to ensure that consumers were insulated from a major price shock and take care of October FCA as well. “This is a government decision,” he said.

Nepra’s member tariff, Amina Ahmed, welcomed the decision and promised to complete regulatory “due diligence as soon as possible”.

“The concept is very welcome,” she said, but added that technical review would follow as soon as the regulator received the formal policy guidance from the government.

The Power Division, in its statement, said the national average electricity tariff inclusive of taxes stood at Rs53.04 per unit while industrial tariff was at Rs62.99 per unit when the current government assumed office in March 2024.

“Through concerted efforts and key policy and reform initiatives, the government successfully reduced the national average tariff by Rs8.76 per unit to Rs44.28 per unit by March 2026, prior to the onset of the Iran-US war and the ensuing energy crisis in the Middle East.

“The reduction in industrial tariffs was even more significant, declining by Rs18.49 per unit from Rs62.99 to Rs44.50 per unit over the same period.”

However, the Iran-US war triggered a sharp increase in international fuel prices, particularly RLNG and coal, exerting upward pressure on monthly FCAs, it said.

“The Power Division closely monitored the evolving situation and implemented a carefully planned and publicly announced load management strategy while optimising the utilisation of available fuel supplies to limit the impact of rising fuel costs on FCAs,” the statement said.

Consequently, during April–September 2026, consumers were protected from a potential additional FCA increase of Rs6–7 per unit, the Power Division claimed.

“The combined FCA and Quarterly Tariff Adjustment (QTA) increase during this period was restricted to an average of Rs2.38 per unit, inclusive of taxes.”

The Power Division said the onset of winter further intensified these challenges.

“A seasonal decline in hydropower generation increases reliance on thermal generation, with thermal fuels accounting for over 80pc of the generation mix during certain winter months. This seasonal shift traditionally results in higher fuel costs.

“In the prevailing circumstances, the elevated international fuel prices following the Iran-US war posed an additional risk of a substantial increase in monthly FCAs.”

Therefore, it came up with the FFCA mechanism wherein the increase due to the above situation would be limited to approximately Rs0.83 per unit (inclusive of taxes) for the period October–December 2026 over the September 2026 FCA, the statement added.

Following the requisite approvals, the Power Division will issue policy guidelines to Nepra for the implementation of the FFCA mechanism, it stated.

“These measures reflect the government’s continued commitment to maintaining tariff stability and minimising the impact of external fuel price shocks on electricity consumers,” the Power Division highlighted.

For the business community, in particular, greater predictability in electricity prices provided an improved basis for planning operational costs and business decisions, while reducing uncertainty arising from monthly tariff adjustments, it added.

“The government remains committed to protecting consumers and supporting economic activity during these challenging times.

“The Power Division will continue to closely monitor developments in international fuel markets and take all necessary measures to safeguard consumer interests,” the statement concluded.

articles.title: Police use tear gas to disperse fresh Bangladesh garment worker protests
articles.summary:
Bangladesh police said they fired tear gas shells and used sound grenades to disperse protesting garment workers who tried ​to block a major highway on Thursday to press ‌their demand for better wages.

The fresh protest broke out a day after a six-member panel approved a 36 per cent increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, ​the smallest in four decades, despite weeks of protests and calls ​for the sum to be doubled.

Protesters also set fire ⁠to a police motorcycle in Gazipur, one of Bangladesh’s major ​garment manufacturing hubs, which has been at the centre of the ​workers’ agitation, police said, adding that peace had since been restored.

“The situation is now calm, but we remain on alert,” said Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of ​Gazipur Industrial Police.

Weeks of protests by garment workers have shuttered ​factories, blocked highways, damaged property and disrupted production in a sector that employs ‌more ⁠than four million people in a country of around 175m.

The government-appointed wage board’s decision, which came in the early hours of Wednesday after nearly 12 hours of talks between workers’ and employers’ ​representatives, did little ​to ease tensions, ⁠with protests breaking out within hours of the announcement.

Labour rights advocates said the increase fell well ​short of workers’ demands and would not provide a ​living ⁠wage.

The garment workers’ protests, along with separate political tensions and violence sparked by former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s plan to return to Dhaka from ⁠self-imposed ​exile in India, have fuelled fears of ​renewed instability in the South Asian country, the world’s second-largest garment exporter after China.

articles.title: JUI-F chief Maulana Fazl among nine party leaders barred from Sargodha district for 30 days
articles.summary:
LAHORE: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman is among nine party leaders barred from entering, residing or remaining in Sargodha district for 30 days, according to a notification issued by the deputy commissioner.

The development came as the party was scheduled to hold a rally in Sargodha on Nov 26 (Thursday).

The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, states that the restriction was imposed under Section 7(1) of the West Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, read with the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008, and would remain in force for 30 days from Nov 25.

Besides Maulana Fazlur Rehman, whose district is listed as Dera Ismail Khan, the notification names eight other party leaders: Maulana Naseer Ahmad Abrar, Maulana Amjad Khan and Prof Ghazanfar Aziz, all from Lahore; Maulana Safi Ullah from Bhakkar; Maulana Muhammad Noor Khan Hans from Multan; Maulana Muhammad Zakria Shah from Faisalabad; Maulana Muhammad Yahya Abbasi from Muzaffargarh; and Maulana Jamal Abdul Nasir from Dera Ghazi Khan.

According to the notification, the deputy commissioner reviewed a report submitted by the Sargodha district police officer and expressed concerns that the individuals had a history of delivering provocative and objectionable speeches that could threaten public order.

It described them as “firebrand speakers” whose speeches were allegedly provocative and inflammatory, adding that they were likely to assemble crowds unlawfully and incite public sentiment against the state and its institutions.

The order further stated that their presence could create a law and order situation and pose a potential threat to peace and security.

Meanwhile, several senior JUI-F leaders were detained in Sargodha and served notices for allegedly violating Section 144, police said. Several local JUI-F leaders were also detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Khushab district.

Separately, the JUI-F chief, in a video message, said that despite the road restrictions and blockade, he was leaving for Sargodha.

He demanded that the government immediately remove all restrictions, release detained party leaders and workers and ensure that constitutional rights and civil liberties be protected.

JUI-F Punjab spokesperson, Hafiz Ghazanfar Aziz, said the government was continuing its “high-handed tactics” against the party.

Aziz claimed that a large number of party workers had been stranded on the road and that arrests were being made across Punjab, with cases registered against JUI-F activists.

Fazl-govt rift

On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

The JUI-F chief was scheduled to participate in a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association on Tuesday. However, he could not leave his residence in a private housing society on Multan Road due to the deployment of a heavy police contingent.

The development came after tensions persisted between JUI-F and the Centre. Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks.

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

A JUI-F spokesman had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

articles.title: PIA restores UK flight operations after Norse Atlantic disruption
articles.summary:
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Thursday that it had restored normal flight operations to and from the United Kingdom, a day after two flights were cancelled by wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic as passengers prepared to board.

Norse Atlantic abruptly suspended operations on Wednesday, saying its financial situation was “critical” and it needed new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

In a press release on Thursday, PIA said: “Flight operations between Pakistan and the United Kingdom have been restored following yesterday’s cancellations by our wet-lease partner.”

The airline said its teams assisted all passengers in both London and Manchester and that passengers affected by the flight cancellations had been re-accommodated on subsequent flights “in accordance with their individual travel preferences”.

“Passengers who opted to alter or defer their travel plans due to the disruption have been facilitated with full, penalty-free refunds,” it added.

The statement said that in line with the contingency plan activated last night, the airline had “transitioned its UK operations directly onto its own widebody Boeing 777 fleet”.

“Today’s scheduled UK services and operations are running on schedule,” the airline added.

In yesterday’s statement, PIA said flights PK786 from London Heathrow to Islamabad, scheduled for 7:55pm GMT, and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore, scheduled for 7pm GMT, were cancelled.

“Notice of this operational suspension was communicated to PIA without any prior warning just as passengers were preparing to board their respective flights in London and Manchester,” the airline’s spokesperson said.

It termed the abrupt suspension of Norse Atlantic’s operations without notice “deeply regrettable” and said it was pursuing the matter with the carrier at the “highest contractual and executive levels”.

PIA was privatised in December last year through an auction. A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for a 75 per cent stake in the airline, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion. The Arif Habib-led consortium had vowed to transform the loss-making airline through operational restructuring, fleet expansion, and improved customer service.

In October, the airline signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aims to meet rising demand.

Following Norse Atlantic’s announcement on Wednesday about its financial situation, its shares plummeted by 76 per cent at 1:03pm GMT. Most of the airline’s market value has already been wiped out this year.

The Norwegian company is now in talks to secure short-term financing, it said in a statement.

“However, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution,” Norse said. It did not say how long it could still operate without new financing.

The carrier, which does not hedge its jet fuel needs, cut capacity as costs skyrocketed following the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February. Many other airlines are faced with the same problem, filing for bankruptcy or initiating restructuring proceedings to survive.

He questioned why political gatherings were banned when Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz herself was holding rallies.

“Do opposition parties not have the right to hold such gatherings?” he asked.
