articles.title: PM Shehbaz launches ‘Mehfooz Dawa’ app to combat counterfeit and substandard medicines
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday launched the “Mehfooz Dawa” app to prevent the circulation of counterfeit and substandard medicines, calling it “a major milestone” and saying the initiative would help restore public confidence in the healthcare system.

The prime minister said education and healthcare facilities should be equally accessible to every citizen and stressed that the federal and provincial governments must work together to ensure the availability of affordable, quality medicines.

The prime minister was speaking at the launch ceremony of the Ministry of National Health Services’ “Mehfooz Dawa” app, which was developed to track medicines.

Federal Minister for National Health Services Mustafa Kamal and Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP) Chief Executive Officer Dr Obaidullah also addressed the event.

Addressing the ceremony, PM Shehbaz hailed the development, describing it as “an extremely magnificent moment” for Pakistan’s medical facilities.

He recalled a 2012 incident at the Punjab Institute of Cardiology in which counterfeit medication was blamed for the deaths of more than 100 patients. At the time, DRAP had maintained that the medication was genuine; however, international testing found that the medicine administered to the patients was intended to treat malaria.

He called for “learning from the past and preparing ourselves” for the future. The prime minister lauded Kamal’s efforts and directed his ministry to work with the IT and Information ministries to raise public awareness about the app.

“History will remember this step in golden words,” the premier remarked.

Noting the application’s mechanism, the premier said it was an “excellent intervention”.

“But the real point is that, to make medicines affordable for the common man, their prices should be in line with what ordinary people can afford,” he said, stressing that obtaining medicines was a “huge challenge” for millions of people in the country.

The prime minister further said: “The founding principle of our policies should be that health and education are equal for everyone and no one should have to go begging and pleading at anyone’s door.”

Speaking at the ceremony, the health minister said the application had been developed with the aim of “protecting innocent lives”. He also noted a “lack of trust” among the public when it came to obtaining medicines.

He praised the pharmaceutical industry’s cooperation, adding that building a database covering around 92,000 medicines and involving more than 700 companies had been an “uphill task”.

Dr Obaidullah explained that the app sought to address three issues: counterfeit medicines, shortages and quality compliance.

The application has three features — medicine verification, complaints and shortage reporting, he said.

By scanning a medicine’s batch number, which would then be checked against a database, users can verify whether the product is authentic, he said. The application will display a green screen if the medicine is genuine and a red screen if it is counterfeit.

If a medicine is found to be counterfeit, consumers will have the option to lodge a complaint. He added that DRAP’s database, which is linked to the application, contains details of around 92,000 medicines.

Users will also be able to report medicine shortages through the application, the DRAP chief said. He added that the government had provided citizens with “protected public health” through the application.

Earlier this month, Drap’s spokesperson Sajid Shah had said the track-and-trace system became operational on October 9.

The idea of introducing a barcode system was first proposed in 2015. It was approved by the federal cabinet in 2017; however, bureaucratic delays prevented its implementation.

Earlier, Kamal, taking notice of the delay, announced that the system would be launched as soon as possible.

Earlier this year, Drap had set October 1 as the cut-off date for launching the barcode system to curb the sale of counterfeit and expired medicines and eradicate black marketing.

Shah said the Ministry of National Health Services was “dedicated” to ensuring that citizens had access to high-quality and effective therapeutic products.

articles.title: US clears SpaceX to launch up to 1 million orbital data-center satellites
articles.summary:
The Trump administration authorised Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Wednesday to launch up to one million satellites as part of its plan to build data centres in space, raising concerns from some experts.

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said SpaceX’s Starmind constellation would “process massive amounts of data to be used back here on Earth.”

The company’s authorisation runs until 2040, according to a document published on the FCC’s website.

“America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement, using Trump’s moniker for artificial intelligence.

He added that data centres would be “essential to sustaining America’s leadership in SI.” Projects for orbiting data centres have multiplied over the past year.

Alongside SpaceX and its Starmind constellation, Google is pursuing its own initiative under the codename “Suncatcher,” while Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin has submitted an application to the FCC for its “Project Sunrise.”

Several startups are also in the race, including Starcloud, which successfully operated an advanced processor known as a GPU aboard a satellite in late 2025. Google also reached that milestone in October.

SpaceX has the advantage of having its own rockets that have already completed hundreds of missions.

In August, Musk promised a first SpaceX satellite launch into orbit in the fourth quarter of 2027 and a ramp-up in 2028.

The company has struck a deal with Nvidia, which will supply its latest-generation Vera Rubin processors, specially designed to operate in space.

‘Disheartened and dismayed’

Most space-based data centre projects have a similar architecture: a constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO), positioned close together to ensure reliable connections between them.

Starmind’s satellites will communicate with those already in orbit as part of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet network, which will then relay the data to Earth.

Other competing networks plan to receive data directly from Earth and send it back using lasers.

But experts have warned of technical obstacles, as well as environmental concerns.

Unresolved technical challenges include processors’ ability to withstand the high levels of radiation in space.

Observers also point to the difficulty of withstanding extreme temperatures or avoiding damage from space debris and micrometeorites.

The American Astronomical Society (AAS) said it was “disheartened and dismayed” by Wednesday’s decision.

“The proposed constellation would significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities and the ability of astronomers and the public to enjoy and study the night sky,” the AAS said in a statement.

It noted that the constellation “involves larger (and therefore brighter) and more numerous objects,” meaning the satellites would “be visible as extremely bright objects for longer periods in the night sky.”

“Drastically expanding satellites in space has a direct impact on people’s everyday lives as well as the future of our planet,” Jan Hasselman, a senior attorney at the nonprofit group Earthjustice, said in a statement.

However, there are numerous advantages to locating a data centre in space over building one on Earth.

Among those, a satellite in what is known as a sun-synchronous orbit can capture solar energy continuously and with eight times the efficiency of its ground-based equivalent.

SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion.

articles.title: Major economies balk at new US tariffs over 'unfair' trade
articles.summary:
Major economies from China to the European Union hit out at proposed US tariffs after Washington concluded its months-long probe into alleged excess production, potentially opening a new phase in trade tensions with both allies and foes alike.

The new tolls, which follow an investigation launched days after the Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s previous duties, range up to 20 per cent and face a period of public comment before taking effect, at the earliest in January.

The levies target some of the United States’ largest trading partners, with China, the EU, India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam in the crosshairs.

A senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, noted that the proposals sought to take existing trade deals into account.

China is among those facing a 20 per cent tariff, but US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the levies were within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing.

“China understands that we’re going to have some level of tariffs. This falls within that understanding,” he told US broadcaster CNBC, adding that Washington was offering China exemptions on around $30 billion of goods.

Beijing hit out at the proposed tariffs on Thursday, warning that it could take “necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests.”

Chinese commerce ministry spokesman He Yadong told a regular briefing that citing “overcapacity” — mass production at a loss to flood overseas markets and undercut local rivals — as a reason to impose tariffs was a “pretext for protectionism.”

He urged Washington “to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation.”

‘Real concern’

Along with other countries, Japan denied having excessive production.

“Japan does not have any non-market policy practices or structural excess production capacity … It is regrettable that a proposed measure targeting Japan has been announced in spite of this,” top government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.

The EU said it rejected the premise of the new tariffs and expected the United States to stick by a deal struck last year.

“The EU and the US share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action,” European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said.

And Singapore said it was “very disappointed” with the proposals, and denied it was protecting its domestic market or subsidising manufacturing.

Vietnam also faces a 20pc tariff; Cambodia and Indonesia 18pc; and India 17pc, according to the US trade representative’s office.

The EU, South Korea and Taiwan, which have signed trade deals with the United States, will see tariffs broadly capped at 15pc.

In a separate announcement, the trade representative also proposed additional tariffs on goods from Brazil, including aircraft, over alleged inaction on addressing US trade concerns.

The Brazilian president’s office called the measures “unacceptable” and said Brasilia would “not yield to this type of threat”.

Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in the country.

Overcapacity concerns affect a range of sectors, from batteries to cement and chemicals to processed food, the senior US official said.

‘Hollowing out’

The duties could add further pressure on US businesses already squeezed by earlier tariffs, with firms now more likely to pass on expenses to consumers already frustrated with the high cost of living.

Affordability was a key issue in this month’s US midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both chambers of Congress by Democrats.

The announcement came as data showed the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge at a three-year high in October, adding to pressure to hike interest rates.

Trade lawyer Ryan Majerus told AFP that he expected the production probe to be among “the most important” actions for the Trump administration, given its underlying concern that factories with excess capacity start operations abroad and “never get turned off, even if there’s no demand.”

This could potentially lead to an oversupply of goods, depressed prices and a “hollowing out” of US manufacturing, he added.

While the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s global tariffs in February, his sector-specific duties remain intact.

The new levies will not stack on top of those sector-specific tariffs on items like automobiles and steel, the senior US official said.

In July, Trump imposed a separate wave of tariffs on 60 economies, accusing them of insufficient action against forced labour.

For economies facing both the forced labour and excess production tariffs, the levies would not stack up and the higher rate would prevail, the US official said.

articles.title: ‘To the moon and beyond’: PM says Shenzhou-24 mission ‘living proof’ of Pak-China friendship
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday described the Shenzhou-24 mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister made the remarks during a meeting with Chinese Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, who called on him at the Prime Minister House.

On Wednesday, Wing Comm­ander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic milestone in Pakistan’s space ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to expand its space diplomacy.

The first Pakistani to travel into orbit, part of the three-member crew of the Shenzhou-24 mission, is serving as a payload specialist and is expected to remain at the station for five to 10 days.

On Thursday, PM Shehbaz met the Chinese envoy and congratulated him and China’s people and leadership on the successful launch.

The prime minister highlighted that Pakistan was “grateful” to China for the opportunity to be part of this historic mission, through which a Pakistani had become the first foreign astronaut to visit China’s space station, the statement said.

“The prime minister said that this was not merely the journey of an individual astronaut, but that of 240 million Pakistanis, embodying, in particular, the dreams and aspirations of the country’s youth and scientific community,” the statement said.

He described the mission as “living proof of the ironclad friendship” between Pakistan and China, adding that cooperation between the two countries had now “truly reached the stars”.

The prime minister expressed his appreciation to the relevant Chinese institutions for training Pakistani astronauts and paid tribute to Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco), academic institutions, scientists and the armed forces for their contributions to this historic achievement.

He said that the achievement would inspire Pakistan’s youth to “aim for the moon and beyond”.

The prime minister requested the ambassador to convey his warm greetings and best wishes to President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang.

“He paid rich tribute to the dynamic leadership and sagacious vision of President Xi, under which China has made remarkable strides in science, technology and space exploration and has opened its space programme to friendly countries for the benefit of humanity,” the statement said.

He underlined that Pakistan remained unwavering in its commitment to work hand in hand with China for the peaceful exploration and utilisation of outer space, it added.

The two sides also reviewed bilateral relations, including activities organised to commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year. PM Shehbaz also handed over congratulatory letters addressed to President Xi and Premier Li to the Chinese ambassador, the statement concluded.

articles.title: IHC extends stay on Islamabad LG polls for two weeks
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday extended its interim order suspending local government elections in the federal capital by another two weeks and sought para-wise comments from the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP).

Justice Umair Majeed Malik was hearing petitions challenging the delimitation of constituencies for Islamabad’s local government elections.

During the hearing, Barrister Adil Aziz Qazi appeared on behalf of the petitioners. The ECP’s counsel informed the court that the commission had suspended the election schedule following the court’s stay order.

Justice Malik observed that the issue of delimitation had not been resolved, questioning how elections could be held when, according to the petitioners, a particular ward had only two voters.

The judge asked the ECP officials to explain whether the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the 2015 law.

The ECP’s counsel submitted that the commission had issued a detailed order explaining the reasons behind its decision. He said the commission had conducted the delimitation exercise six times in accordance with the relevant law.

The court observed that if the commission had initiated proper proceedings, an appeal could have been filed against its decision. It also questioned whether the ECP could still alter the delimitations after issuing the election schedule.

Justice Malik remarked that the commission would have to satisfy the court that the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the law. He noted that several petitions had previously been filed over the matter.

The judge also observed that the petitioners claimed they did not even know which wards they belonged to.

The ECP’s counsel maintained that the commission had carried out the delimitation exercise in accordance with the applicable law and issued an order on October 14 declaring the process complete.

The court sought a detailed response from the ECP and adjourned the proceedings for two weeks.

Two weeks ago, Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad.

The local government elections in Islamabad have faced numerous delays and postponements since the term of the last local government expired in February 2021.

The ECP has issued multiple schedules, only to cancel them later for various reasons, including legislative changes and court orders. The delimitation of constituencies and union councils was carried out six times, while the election schedule was issued four times.

The ECP had decided that, since the local government law enacted in 2015 was still in force, elections would be held under the Act. This meant polls would be held in 50 constituencies, after which the mayor and deputy mayors would be elected.

After the completion of various stages of the electoral process, it had decided that polling would be held on Dec 20. The ECP had reserved four days, from December 21 to 24, for the consolidation of results.

articles.title: Rawalpindi ATC defers verdict in November 2024 protest case involving Aleema Khan until Dec 16
articles.summary:
RAWALPINDI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Rawalpindi on Thursday adjourned until December 16 the announcement of its reserved verdict in a case registered against Aleema Khan, sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, in connection with the November 26, 2024 protest.

ATC Judge Amjad Ali Shah deferred the verdict for the sixth time without holding any further proceedings.

Aleema’s counsel, Faisal Malik, appeared before the court on Thursday.

The court had reserved its verdict in the case on September 22, fixing Sept 25 as the announcement date. However, the announcement was deferred after Judge Shah went on leave, with October 1 set as the next date.

The verdict has since been postponed several times, with the latest adjournment pushing it to Dec 16.

Aleema’s counsel had also objected to the court reserving its verdict without hearing the defence’s arguments, saying he had not been given an opportunity to present his case.

In September, Aleema was detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance ahead of a PTI march towards Islamabad. She remains incarcerated at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail.

The case

The case came to be known as the November 26 protest case. The protest saw more than 10,000 PTI supporters enter Islamabad in 2024, defying a ban on public gatherings and a lockdown, and clash with around 20,000 security personnel deployed to prevent them from advancing.

A day of clashes between security forces and protesters in the city’s Red Zone ended with the PTI leadership retreating, after which the party announced that it was calling off its planned protest sit-in “for the time being”.

Subsequently, cases were registered against several PTI leaders under various sections of the Pakistan Penal Code and Section 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act. Two of the cases were registered at Taxila police station and one each at Sadiqabad and Naseerabad police stations.

Aleema, along with 10 others, was booked in the case registered at Sadiqabad police station.

articles.title: Egypt says 31 dead in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns
articles.summary:
A fire erupted in Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday killing at least 31 people, the health ministry said, after a fuel truck reportedly overturned on a packed highway.

AFP footage showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists sounded their horns and scrambled to get away. Surrounding buildings appeared to escape the flames.

State media reported that the fire broke out when a truck loaded with fuel overturned on Cairo’s Ring Road — a crowded highway linking different parts of the capital — and burst into flames, engulfing nearby vehicles.

The health ministry said 39 ambulances were sent to the scene and 15 people were taken to hospital with injuries, four of them in critical condition.

“The scene was terrifying,” Abdel Rahman Khalil told AFP, saying he arrived shortly after the crash and saw the overturned fuel truck engulfed in flames.

AFP images showed a grisly aftermath with cars burned out, as firefighters doused the truck’s wreckage.

Egypt’s public prosecutor said an investigation had been opened and DNA tests were being carried out to identify badly burned victims.

The health ministry said it had raised its emergency alert level and Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar had travelled to the scene and nearby hospitals.

Charred wreckage

The health minister’s spokesman told state-linked Al-Qahera News that “the Ring Road has been reopened, and the remnants of the accident have been cleared.”

Footage carried by Al-Qahera News showed the charred truck’s wreckage being removed, while traffic partially resumed around it.

A spokesperson for the Egyptian Cabinet told local media that Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly had ordered an investigation into the causes of the accident.

He said the government was awaiting a full clarification before determining “future measures regarding the transport of petroleum products and ensuring safety and security during such transport operations”.

Road deaths

Egypt, with its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, has suffered several deadly fires in recent years.

Fire escapes, smoke detectors and alarms are rare and in many areas, warrens of narrow roads make it hard for fire engines to reach disaster sites.

Car crashes are also common, and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted.

Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency.

The year before, more than 5,200 road deaths were recorded across the country, according to authorities.

In August, at least 18 people, many of them teenagers, were killed in northern Egypt when two pick-up trucks carrying agricultural day-labourers crashed.

PM, DPM express condolences

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said he was “deeply grieved by the tragic loss of precious lives”.

In a post on X, he wrote, “On behalf of the people and Government of Pakistan, I extend my heartfelt condolences to President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, the bereaved families and the brotherly people of Egypt.”

Reaffirming Pakistan’s solidarity with Egypt in the hour of grief, he said his thoughts and prayers were with those who had lost their loved ones.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in a post on X, also expressed his condolences for the loss of lives in Cairo.

“Deeply saddened by the tragic loss of precious lives in the fuel tanker fire near Cairo.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and the Government and brotherly people of Egypt,” he wrote.

He added, “Pakistan stands in solidarity with Egypt during this difficult time.”

articles.title: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR
articles.summary:
Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

On November 21, security forces intercepted the movement of terrorists in Sibi district, killing two more, the ISPR said.

In two separate engagements in Panjgur and Kech districts on November 22 and 23, security forces raided terrorist hideouts and killed two more terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan, the ISPR added.

The ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-i-Istehkam”, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

Meanwhile, President Asif Ali Zardari lauded the security forces for carrying out “successful intelligence-based operations” in Balochistan against “terrorists operating under India’s patronage”, a statement issued by his office said.

The statement quoted him as saying: “Security forces’ continued successes in the fight against terrorism demonstrate their commitment and sacrifices for peace and stability in the country.”

He added that the “elimination of Fitna-al-Hindustan and foreign-backed terrorists is essential for national security. Security forces and law enforcement agencies will continue operations against foreign-backed and -supported terrorists in every part of Pakistan”.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. Last week, 15 terrorists were killed during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district.

On Nov 14, four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple IBOs in Balochistan and KP.

On Nov 1, a soldier was martyred while 17 terrorists were killed in two IBOs in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts.

According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, Pakistan recorded fewer terrorist attacks from Nov 6 to 12, but fatalities and injuries increased sharply, “highlighting the changing intensity and continued volatility of militant threat across the country”.

KP remained the principal centre of violence, accounting for 16 attacks and 44 fatalities. Balochistan recorded 13 attacks, resulting in eight deaths and 19 injuries, while the former tribal districts witnessed a “substantial” reduction in attacks.

articles.title: 25 Bajaur youth feared dead as boat capsizes near Libya
articles.summary:
BAJAUR: At least 25 people from Bajaur tribal district are feared dead or missing after a migrant boat capsized near Libya, according to unofficial reports on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, funeral prayers in absentia of several victims were offered in their native areas, which were attended by people from different walks of life.

The participants urged the government and international organisations to help bring their bodies back to their homes at the earliest.

The incident, which has plunged the entire district into utter grief and sorrow since it emerged on social media late Tuesday night, has yet to be officially confirmed by the Pakistani government, international media, or rescue organisations.

However, reports based on the victims’ agents and narrated by their families said the tragic incident involving a migrant boat en route to Europe reportedly happened in the Mediterranean Sea near Libya on November 21, 2026.

“It is true that this tragic incident has yet to be confirmed by both the Pakistani and Italian governments, nor reported by international media, but according to the victims’ agents who were in close contact with their families, it happened last Saturday, November 21,” said Nasir Khan, a resident of Lowi Mamund tehsil, to which many of the victims belonged.

Javed Khan, an elder of Larkholozo area of Lowi Mamund, while speaking to Dawn, also confirmed that about 11 victims were from the region.

According to reports, the number of victims could be about 35, most of them youngsters aged between 20 and 27, belonging to Lowi Mamund and Salarzai tehsils.

However, as per the bereaved families, based on information from the victims’ agents, 25 people have been confirmed dead in the incident.

According to the victims’ list available with Dawn, Wahidullah, Rahatullah, Pazirullah, Nimatullah, Sher Dad, Abdul Manan and Izharullah belonged to different areas of Salarzai tehsil.

The list mentioned that Mansoor, Irshad, Arifullah, Zakir, Sulaiman, Nematullah, Asif, Junaid, Latif Khan, Muhammad Saliman, Mohammad Khan, Salahuddin, Sanaullah, Bilal Khan, Inayat Khan, Inayatullah, Junaid Khan and Jalal Khan belonged to separate localities of Lowi Mamund tehsil.

The incident has yet to be officially confirmed by the federal government, the Foreign Office, or any international organisation regarding its circumstances and the number of victims.

However, according to a report by BBC Urdu, an official of the Pakistani embassy in Libya told its correspondent that he was not aware of the incident and had learned about it through the news reports.

The official, however, said that they had sought reports regarding the incident from the Libyan authorities and the UN organisation, the International Organisation for Migration, which have yet to confirm the incident.

Meanwhile, Mubarak Zeb Khan, MNA from Bajaur and Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Tribal Districts, whose cousin Pazirullah was also among the victims, said on Wednesday that he was in close contact with officials at the Pakistani embassy and the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis over the incident.

In a social media post, Mubarak Zeb Khan mentioned that a search operation for the missing victims was under way to recover the bodies.

Meanwhile, PTI MPAs Anwar Zeb Khan, Dr Hamidur Rehman and Ajmal Khan and ANP MPA Mohammad Nisar Khan, PML-N leader Shahabuddin Khan, and JI leader Sahibzada Haroon Rasheed and Samar Haroon Bilour, adviser to the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on information and public relations, expressed sorrow over the tragic deaths.

ANP spokesperson Arslan Khan Nazim said that it was deeply tragic and a national calamity that more than 30 young people from Bajaur, who had left home dreaming of better prospects and jobs, drowned in the sea near Libya.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: Anthropic chief denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
articles.summary:
Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on Wednesday denied wanting humanity to give up its free will to AI, calling it “absurd” to attribute the idea to him as rival tech leaders push back.

“No, I do not believe that we should ‘surrender human free will’ to AI systems, and it’s absurd to suggest that I do,” Amodei wrote in a lengthy post on X, a week after Anthropic’s record-setting stock market debut.

“We should never sacrifice legitimacy or self-determination at the altar of efficiency or security,” he added.

Fears that AI tools could slip out of human control have haunted Silicon Valley since a string of incidents this summer, including the hacking of Hugging Face by autonomous AI agents developed by OpenAI.

“We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!” an Anthropic safety lead, Evan Hubinger, wrote in September.

Amodei took aim, without naming names, at “some AI CEOs” who repeat slogans like “AI should be just a tool” but then are not “actually doing anything different in their products.”

On Sunday, Meta’s Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang wrote on X that “we should not be okay with a ‘handover’ of society to AI.”

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said earlier this month that if the tradeoff for curing cancer is “you are going to lose all agency and control and voice in the future,” that is “a terrible sales pitch.” Amodei’s post was in response to an article by US outlet Axios on AI debate, though he did not address his previous remarks on the topic.

In February, Amodei told The New York Times that in “life-critical, safety-critical cases, we really want to turn it over” to AI.

And in late 2024, he predicted that AI systems “will be the leaders, and they’ll be ordering humans or other AI systems around.” On Wednesday, he acknowledged that “we may want limits” on recursive self-improvement, or RSI, in which AI models can autonomously create new versions of itself, and that “we don’t expect it to be safe for Claude to build successive frontier models fully autonomously,” without saying where the line should be drawn.

Yet in its IPO filing, Anthropic said that “each new version of a Claude model directly accelerates development of the next,” and that Claude wrote over 90 per cent of the contributions to its codebase in September.

Elon Musk, who has long predicted that superintelligent AI would leave humans “like pet Labradors,” reposted Amodei’s statement with a one-word comment: “interesting.”

articles.title: Lahore High Court seeks police report on Maulana Fazl’s confinement
articles.summary:
LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Wednesday sought a report from the capital police chief on a petition challenging the alleged confinement of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to his temporary residence in the city.

Justice Ali Zia Bajwa heard the petition filed by Advocate Chaudhry Abrar Hussain, a member of the JUI-F legal wing.

The lawyer informed the court that Maulana Fazl had been restricted to his residence in Lahore.

The judge observed that if the JUI-F chief had been illegally detained, the matter was serious and whoever was responsible for the unlawful action would have to face the consequences.

Judge warns of consequences if JUI-F chief illegally detained

Justice Bajwa remarked that if Maulana Fazl had been placed under detention, the authorities would have to provide reasons for the action.

Additional Advocate General Farrukh Javed Lodhi told the court that the petitioner-lawyer had met Maulana Fazl the other day. He said a photograph of the meeting had gone viral on social media.

Advocate Hussain said he had been allowed to meet the JUI-F chief after repeatedly requesting the police for permission. He maintained that Maulana Fazl remained under illegal confinement at his residence and was still not allowed to leave the house.

The petitioner contended that the JUI-F chief’s life and liberty were under threat. He sought directions for his recovery.

The judge directed the Capital City Police Officer to submit a detailed report on the matter by Thursday (today).

The JUI-F chief was scheduled to participate in a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association on Tuesday. However, he could not leave his residence in a private housing society on Multan Road due to deployment of a heavy police contingent.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: PTI disowns Achakzai’s call for national govt
articles.summary:
• Salman Akram, Ali Zafar exchange heated words at parliamentary party meeting
• Party to deliberate on new provinces only after reviewing government’s draft

ISLAMABAD: The PTI on Wednesday distanced itself from a proposal made by Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai regarding formation of a national government in the country.

After a joint meeting of the parliamentary groups of the PTI in the National Assembly and the Senate, one of the participants told Dawn that they discussed the recent statement of Mr Achakzai in which he had proposed formation of a national government in the country and a majority of the members opposed such an idea.

“After a detailed discussion, it was collectively decided that this proposal belongs to Achakzai’s party [Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party], and the PTI will not support any such move,” the participant said on condition of anonymity.

Mr Achakzai had called for a national government and constitutional reforms during a multi-party conference at the Lahore High Court Bar Association.

Sources revealed that in the meeting it had been decided that no party member would issue any policy statement on the issue of new provinces until the government releases its draft proposal.

The party’s parliamentarians decided to have an in-house discussion on the new provinces’ issue sometime next week to finalise its stance.

According to the sources, the meeting was interrupted for a brief time due to exchange of heated arguments betw­e­en party’s Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and parliamentary leader in the Senate Barrister Ali Zafar.

They said Mr Zafar flared up when Mr Raja stated that he was aware that “what some persons are doing but does not want to mention their names”.

Mr Zafar challenged Mr Raja to mention the names. At this point, the two leaders exchanged some heated arguments when some of the participants, including Aamir Dogar and Faisal Gandapur, intervened and prevented the situation from getting worse.

Without naming, Mr Raja said some of the party members even did not bother to read party’s policy statements due to which each of them started giving different statements.

He said that despite being underground, Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram issued policy statements on a daily basis, and sent them the party’s narrative but they did not read it.

The sources said that PTI’s Sardar Latif Khosa briefed the participants about his recent meeting with the party’s founding chairman Imran Khan in Adiala jail.

Mr Khosa reportedly said that Mr Khan had directed him that the issue of new provinces should be discussed in the parliamentary party meeting.

Meanwhile, talking to Dawn, Sheikh Waqas Akram said the PTI would give its official reaction after analysing the government’s draft for new provinces. He said it had been decided that a coordination committee would be formed to take prompt decisions. The committee, he said, would comprise representatives of the National Assembly, Senate and provincial parliamentary parties.

Meeting with Imran

Meanwhile, the PTI has submitted a list of the party members with the Adiala jail administration for a meeting with Mr Khan today (Thursday). The Islamabad High Court has ordered to arrange the meeting of family and lawyers with Mr Khan on Tuesdays and meeting of PTI leaders on Thursdays.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: PM stresses IT potential for economic growth
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday reiterated the government’s commitment to harnessing Pakistan’s IT export potential as a key driver of economic growth and youth employment.

He stressed that attracting domestic and foreign investment into the IT and IT-enabled services sectors remained a priority, directing authorities to ensure technology zones function strictly as hubs for innovation and export growth.

At a review meeting on the information technology and telecommunication sectors, the prime minister directed the formation of a committee to conduct a third-party audit of all operational IT parks under the Special Technology Zones Authority (STZA).

The prime minister also called for a comprehensive review of STZA laws to prevent the potential misuse of corporate establishment provisions.

During the briefing, officials informed the meeting that Alibaba was developing a comprehensive ‘Super App’ for the government of Pakistan under the Strategic Transformative Framework, which will consolidate all public-facing government services onto a single digital platform.

Orders third-party audit to stop misuse of tech zones; directs faster privatisation of loss-making SOEs

Reviewing sector-wide performance, the ministry reported that Pakistan’s IT exports stood at $4.6 billion in FY26 ending June 30, with an additional $1.24bn recorded in the July-September quarter of FY27. Freelance exports reached $1.165bn in FY26.

It was reported that the number of IT companies had surged, while the functioning of digital public services was also enhanced. The meeting was further informed that 32 technology zones were being developed across seven clusters nationwide, with 21 operational and 11 under construction.

Around 300 tech firms have set up operations in these zones, bringing in Rs100bn in realised investment, while projects worth Rs105bn were in the pipeline.

Loss-making SOEs

Chairing a separate meeting to review progress on the privatisation of state-owned enterprises and assets, the prime minister directed the relevant authorities to identify additional loss-making SOEs for divestment.

The premier said privatising non-functional SOEs and assets was vital to improving the national economy, reducing the burden on the national exchequer, and ensuring economic stability.

He underlined that privatising loss-making SOEs would create opportunities to redirect national resources toward public welfare and development projects.

The prime minister directed that the privatisation process for state entities be accelerated and that all projects be completed within the stipulated timelines. “Legal hurdles must not be allowed to delay the privatisation process, and effective measures should be taken to resolve them,” the prime minister said.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: Diesel price dips below Rs350 after 4 months; petrol rate down by Rs4
articles.summary:
The government reduced the price of diesel by Rs5 per litre and that of petrol by Rs4 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs314 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs348 per litre on Nov 26 (Thursday).

The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: Plateau: 16 killed, four injured in fresh attack
articles.summary:
From Jude Owuamanam, Jos

No fewer than 16 people have been killed and four others seriously injured after gunmen identified as Fulani herdsmen attacked Tafi Gariesna, a hamlet of Kyie Ihwien, near Jebbu Miango in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The attackers were said to have invaded the community at 11:30pm on Wednesday, shooting randomly. By the early morning of Thursday, 16 people had been identified as dead, while the four injured were rushed to hospital for urgent medical attention.

According to the Irigwe Development Association (IDA) and the traditional council of Irigwe land, the following casualties were identified.

They included Moses Oko, 70; Maingwa Zere Rangya, 60; Danladi Ishaku, 45; Luka Danladi, 21; Elisha Luka, 18; and David Danladi, 10.

Others were Ishaya Goslow, 18; Lami Danladi, 30; Isi Ishaku, 18; Zhime Ngaza, 75; ThankGod Danladi, 18; Gideon Joseph, 25; and Ladi Abba, 65.

Ruth Istifanus, 20; Mary Keyi, 18; and 13-year-old Lazarus Musa were also among those killed.

The Public Relations Officer of the IDA, Sam Jugo, in a statement, said: “Irigwe Development Association (IDA) and the traditional council of Irigwe land received the shocking and devastating news of an overnight attack on the residents of Tafi Gariesna, a hamlet of Kyie Ihwien, near Jebbu Miango by 11:30pm of Wednesday 25th November, 2026.

“Eyewitnesses say they heard and saw people of the Fulani extraction. The attackers wielded assault rifles and other dangerous weapons. By dawn of Thursday 26th November, 2026, about 16 persons lay dead while four other survivors were rushed to unknown medical facilities with various degrees of injuries.”

The traditional ruler of the area, Nggwe Gado Dama, confirmed this and added that the matter had been reported to the Divisional Police Headquarters, Bassa, and the Commander, Sector 3 of Operation Enduring Peace.

He said that soldiers had been deployed to the scene to avert further attacks.

The IDA appealed to all natives not to take the law into their own hands but to allow the security agencies to do the needful to dispense justice to the slain.

Military authorities are yet to comment on the incident. The Media Officer of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP), Capt. Chinonso Oteh, could not be reached for comment.

 

The post Plateau: 16 killed, four injured in fresh attack appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: ‘He was inconsolable’: Kenneth Okonkwo reveals Francis Duru’s private agony after losing son
articles.summary:
● Urges people to look beyond appearances and check on friends who may be silently hurting

___________________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Veteran actor-turned-politician Kenneth Okonkwo has revealed the private anguish endured by the late Nollywood actor and filmmaker Francis Duru following the loss of his son, Ifeanyi, recounting a heartbreaking conversation in which the deceased struggled to comprehend his helplessness as a father.

Okonkwo, who disclosed this at Duru’s Night of Tribute at Family Worship Centre, Abuja, on Wednesday, said he had privately reached out to the late actor after the bereavement and was deeply moved by what he told him.

Recounting their conversation, Okonkwo said Duru told him: “I couldn’t believe I could watch my son in such a situation that he is in, and I couldn’t do anything about it.”

The actor said he was making the disclosure publicly for the first time to illustrate the depth of pain people could be carrying beneath an outward appearance of strength and happiness.

“Why I brought this thing out is for you to know why you should be your brother’s keeper. Forget about outward appearance. Let’s take our time to make that call to somebody. He needs it, but he may never admit it,” he said.

Okonkwo said losing a child was an agonising experience that could leave even the strongest person inconsolable.

He recalled another man’s description of the pain as being like “somebody pulling your tooth without anaesthetics”, noting that people who counsel others on grief might only fully understand its depth when confronted with such a loss themselves.

He also referred to the experience of Pastor Enoch Adeboye who, after losing his son, acknowledged that the reality of such grief was different from the words of comfort people ordinarily offered.

Okonkwo’s account offered a rare glimpse into the personal struggles of Duru, who was celebrated at the tribute for his talent, humility, generosity and commitment to family and friends.

Describing the deceased as a brother and a naturally gifted performer, Okonkwo said Duru’s acting talent flowed so effortlessly that reading scripts with him could feel like listening to an ordinary conversation.

“Francis Duru is a very talented natural actor. It flows from him. If you’re reading script with him, at times you think that he’s always conversing. But he’s acting. That tells you the depth of his talent as an actor,” he said.

He described Duru’s humility as legendary, adding that he was unaware of any serious personal enmity between the late actor and his colleagues in Nollywood.

“For somebody that is well known, well-talented, such things are rare,” he said.

Okonkwo said he wished Duru had not died when he did, describing his passing as a painful loss to the entertainment industry and those who knew him.

He urged people not to assume that friends and acquaintances were doing well simply because they appeared cheerful or successful in public, stressing the importance of checking on them and offering support even when they did not ask for it.

Reflecting on the impact of bereavement, he also urged people to draw strength from faith and remember those who would continue to bear the consequences of their absence.

“Look at the ones that will still suffer the impact when you’re not there and use them as consolation,” he said.

He prayed for God’s acceptance of Duru’s soul and for long life for his surviving children, quoting the Bible: “With long life, he will satisfy us and show us his salvation.”

 

The post ‘He was inconsolable’: Kenneth Okonkwo reveals Francis Duru’s private agony after losing son appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: 2027: Bwala accuses Atiku of exploiting poverty, Obi of social media mobilisation
articles.summary:
Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of exploiting economic hardship for political gains, while alleging that former Anambra State governor Peter Obi relies heavily on social media engagement to sustain his popularity.

Bwala described Atiku’s campaign strategy as the “weaponisation of poverty’s algorithm”, while dismissing social media activities and large crowds at campaign rallies as unreliable indicators of electoral strength.

He spoke on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast while responding to questions on whether Tinubu was worried about growing support for Atiku in the North ahead of the January 16 presidential election.

Bwala dismissed crowds at Atiku’s rallies as insufficient evidence of widespread voter support, arguing that the former vice-president had repeatedly attracted large audiences during campaigns without translating such gatherings into electoral victories.

“I am an advocate from day one that numbers in rally is not a proof of popularity. I even cautioned people from our own side that if we go to a place and everywhere is filled, let us not project it as a strength, because we dey on the street we know how people are gathered in campaigns and Atiku is a master in gathering people when it comes to campaign,” he said.

Recalling Atiku’s presidential contest against former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Bwala said the former vice-president gained momentum shortly before the election, with large crowds creating the impression that he could defeat the incumbent.

“I remember the first time he ran on the platform provided by Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu against Obasanjo. It was within few days to election that he was sort of getting some oxygen. If you see everywhere he goes, rave, rave, rave. Everybody believed he was going to defeat Obasanjo. At the end of the day, what is it?” Bwala said.

He argued that political strength should instead be measured by a candidate’s ability to mobilise voters at the grassroots, questioning Atiku’s political structure in the North, particularly as the party he recently joined has no governor.

“But even with the crowd, we have pulled more crowds than him. So what is Atiku Tsunami? What is his structure? Because right now the party he has moved to does not have a governor,” he said.

Bwala also criticised Obi’s political strategy, claiming that the former Anambra governor’s popularity was largely driven by social media activities rather than physical political structures.

He alleged that Obi had lost the support of churches and political allies who played significant roles in his 2023 presidential campaign, claiming some had since withdrawn their backing.

“It’s just like Peter Obi. As I talked about Atiku, he uses social media activities to gauge his election. They are nowhere in Nigeria. In 2023, the church was his structure. They are not with him. Tell me the church he has gone to lately. He has been disinvited,” he said.

The presidential aide further claimed that Obi’s political supporters and structures had abandoned him, leaving social media influencers and content creators to sustain online engagement around his activities.

He said the online attention Obi continued to attract was driven by content creators seeking engagement and revenue rather than being a reflection of his electoral prospects.

“And if you are looking for revenue, you are looking for engagement, believe me, I’m telling you, the best person to pick is Peter Obi, because he’s a mixture of everything that creates engagement for you, so the guys are not losing on social media. So, Peter will lose election, but they will gain,” Bwala said.

Reacting to videos circulating online showing alleged hired rally attendees demanding payment and fighting after campaign events, Bwala reiterated his opposition to using crowd size as a measure of political popularity.

He said elections were determined by registered voters who were accredited, cast their ballots and had their votes counted and transmitted, rather than by social media trends or crowd sizes.

“I have always been an advocate of not using crowd because if you are using crowd, then that should be the new model for determining WHO won the election. But election are won when registered voters, accredited voters, cast their vote, and the vote is counted, and the vote is transmitted, and the vote is collected, and it is then announced. That is the way by which people win election, not the popularity because of the management of algorithm,” he said.

Bwala concluded by contrasting what he described as the political strategies of Atiku and Obi, alleging that the former relied on economic hardship while the latter benefited from online mobilisation.

“What they are doing is that Peter Obi runs the social media algorithm, Atiku runs the weaponization of poverty’s algorithm,” he said.

articles.title: Group petitions NJC over alleged interference in Kano governorship election judgment, APC campaign council rejects petition
articles.summary:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano

A group which identified itself as “Concerned Nigerian Citizens” has petitioned the National Judicial Council (NJC) to investigate alleged interference in the Supreme Court judgment that restored Abba Kabir Yusuf as Governor of Kano State in 2023.

The petition, dated 24 November 2026 and signed by K. Suleiman Malali, Kaduna State, was addressed to the Chairman of the NJC through the office of the Chief Justice of Nigeria.

The petition was copied to the Chief Justice of Nigeria, the President of the Nigerian Bar Association, the Attorney-General of the Federation and the National Assembly Committee on Judiciary.

The petitioners explained that they were acting to protect the integrity, independence and public confidence in the Judiciary, adding that they were not seeking to re-litigate, review or set aside the judgment, which they noted is final by virtue of Section 235 of the Constitution.

According to the petition, the 2023 Kano State governorship election was contested between Yusuf of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) and Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna of the All Progressives Congress (APC). The petitioners recalled that the Election Petition Tribunal and the Court of Appeal nullified Yusuf’s election, before the Supreme Court reversed the decisions and restored him as duly elected governor.

The petitioners said their action followed a recent interview allegedly granted by Governor Yusuf to BBC Hausa, in which he was reported to have said, in substance, that he was instructed by his political mentor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, to negotiate with the President, adding that he swore on the Holy Book that if the President would ensure that judgment was delivered in his favour, they would defect to the APC.

The petitioners said the alleged statements in the interview, if true, raised grave questions of law and judicial ethics, including breach of the Judicial Oath, breach of judicial independence, breach of the Code of Conduct for Judicial Officers, and erosion of public confidence in the Judiciary.

They stated that they were not asserting as fact that any Justice was compromised, but that the allegation was of such gravity that silence by the Council would further erode public confidence in the Judiciary.

The group therefore asked the NJC to constitute an independent panel to investigate the circumstances surrounding the allegation, and to obtain and authenticate the full, unedited recording and certified transcript of the BBC Hausa interview from the BBC.

They also asked the Council to invite Governor Yusuf to confirm or deny, on oath, whether he made the said statements and the full context thereof, and to invite any other person mentioned to respond.

They prayed for a review of the judgment and proceedings in Appeal No. SC/CV/1179/2023 strictly to determine whether the decision was in accordance with law and due process for institutional learning, and to make appropriate findings.

The petitioners further asked that, if any judicial officer was found to have breached the Judicial Oath or Code of Conduct, appropriate disciplinary sanctions should be recommended and, if no misconduct was found, a clear, reasoned public statement should be published exonerating the Justices and reaffirming the independence of the Judiciary.

They concluded that the Judiciary remained the last hope of the common man, and that a judiciary whose judgments were perceived as negotiated, rather than adjudicated, could not command obedience or respect.

Meanwhile, the APC Presidential/Gubernatorial Campaign Council in Kano State has rejected the petition, describing it as misleading, lacking credible evidence and based on a misrepresentation of the governor’s BBC Hausa interview.

In a press statement issued in Kano and signed by its Campaign Spokesperson II, Sanusi Kiru, the council argued that the petitioners had confused a request for presidential non-interference in judicial proceedings with an alleged attempt to influence the outcome of the case.

According to the council, Governor Yusuf had explained in the interview that his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, instructed him to approach President Bola Ahmed Tinubu with an assurance that they would return to the APC if the President refrained from interfering in the legal proceedings concerning the 2023 Kano governorship election and the case ended in their favour.

The APC council maintained that asking the President not to interfere in judicial proceedings was consistent with the constitutional principle of separation of powers and could not, on its own, constitute evidence of judicial compromise.

It challenged the petitioners to identify any Supreme Court Justice allegedly involved in the purported negotiations, provide evidence of unlawful presidential instructions, or establish any improper communication, inducement or threat capable of influencing the judgment.

The council further argued that political discussions and subsequent political realignments could not, without supporting evidence, establish judicial corruption.

It cited the 18 March 2023 governorship election, in which the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) declared Yusuf the winner with 1,019,602 votes against 890,705 votes secured by his closest opponent, giving him a margin of 128,897 votes.

It also recalled that the Supreme Court, in its judgment delivered on 12 January 2024 in Yusuf Abba Kabir v. APC, INEC and NNPP, Appeal No. SC/CV/1179/2023, addressed issues including the validity of 165,616 deducted votes and the jurisdiction of lower courts over questions concerning political party membership.

According to the council, the Supreme Court’s reversal of the lower courts’ decisions was an exercise of its constitutional appellate powers, adding that the petitioners had not demonstrated any connection between the court’s legal reasoning and the alleged political interference.

On the petition’s legal basis, the APC council argued that the NJC lacked the constitutional authority to review or overturn the legal correctness of a Supreme Court judgment. It cited Section 235 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides for the finality of Supreme Court decisions, and argued that the NJC’s disciplinary powers should not be confused with appellate jurisdiction.

The council also questioned the timing and documentation of the petition, noting that it was filed more than 34 months after the Supreme Court judgment. It said the circulated version of the petition contained neither a verifying affidavit nor an authenticated recording or supporting exhibits to substantiate the allegations.

The statement further maintained that the demand for the governor to testify under oath must be considered within the constitutional protections afforded to him under Section 308 of the Constitution.

The APC council urged the NJC to conduct an appropriate preliminary assessment if the petition was formally presented, and to dismiss it if it failed to meet the required legal and evidential standards. It also challenged the petitioners to produce the complete authenticated BBC Hausa interview and credible evidence to support their allegations rather than relying on speculation.

The council said the right to petition constituted authorities must be exercised with factual accuracy, intellectual honesty and respect for established legal procedures.

 

The post Group petitions NJC over alleged interference in Kano governorship election judgment, APC campaign council rejects petition appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: ‘Who will comfort my broken heart?’ Francis Duru’s wife breaks down at tribute night
articles.summary:
● Pastor Sarah Omaku steps in to console grieving widow, as children recall actor’s devotion to family

_______________________________________________________________________

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

The grief was overwhelming. Unable to hold back tears, Adokiye, the wife of the late veteran Nollywood actor and filmmaker Chief Francis Duru, broke down while reading her tribute to him at the Service of Songs and Night of Tribute in Abuja on Wednesday.

As she struggled to continue, Pastor Sarah Omaku stepped in to console her, urging her to breathe and gather strength to finish reading the tribute.

In an emotional account of the void left by her husband’s death, Adokiye described Duru as “my rock, my safe place and the anchor of our family”, admitting that she was completely lost without him.

She wondered who would stand by her, comfort her broken heart over the loss of their son and help her shoulder the responsibility of caring for their children.

Her poignant questions, delivered through tears, brought the pain of the family’s loss into sharp focus, leaving mourners deeply moved.

Despite her grief, Adokiye said the family was trusting God that Duru was finally at peace, pledging to make him proud.

The widow’s emotional tribute was reinforced by the deeply personal accounts of their children, who remembered a father whose fame as a celebrated actor never overshadowed his commitment to his family.

Their son, Sotonye, described Duru as a present father, protector, provider, teacher and confidant, recalling the simple moments they shared, from watching football and Chelsea matches to sharing snacks and praying together.

He said his father, whom he fondly called “my governor”, was actively involved in his life and remained a source of guidance, even in their everyday interactions.

Recalling the last words his father said to him before he left for school, Sotonye said: “Sotonye, you’re becoming a man now. Make sure you take care of your mother and sister.”

The words, he said, had taken on a deeper meaning following his father’s death, which occurred on the day he was due to return home.

Sotonye recalled that he was initially so shocked by the news that he could not cry, struggling to comprehend the loss.

He described being a father as the most beautiful of the many roles his father played, saying Duru’s greatest legacy to him was not his fame but the love, guidance and values he imparted.

His sister, Frances, also remembered a humble and kind father whose celebrity status was hardly noticeable within the family.

She said that, at home, he was simply “Daddy”, recalling how he frequently called to check on his children whenever he was away.

For Frances, her father’s fame did not define the man she knew. At home, she said, he was a caring parent who remained attentive to his children’s needs.

Beyond the family’s tributes, the evening also turned attention to Duru’s Christian faith and his relationship with the church, with speakers recalling how he submitted himself to spiritual guidance and became actively involved in its drama ministry.

Delivering the exhortation, Pastor Wilson Akubo urged mourners to reflect on the brevity of life, warning against the illusion that wealth, fame, influence and personal achievements could guarantee immortality.

Drawing from Ecclesiastes 7:1-4, Akubo said death was an inevitable part of human existence and that the most enduring measure of a person’s life was the legacy he left behind.

He identified three lessons from the occasion: the illusion of immortality, the brevity of life and the need for salvation through Jesus Christ.

Recalling his longstanding friendship with Duru, dating back to their National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) days, Akubo described the late actor as someone who understood the importance of faith and his relationship with God.

He urged those present to embrace Christ, stressing that material possessions, professional accomplishments and social connections could not secure salvation.

Music also formed part of the celebration, with the choir performing two of Duru’s favourite gospel songs, “Fragrance to Fire” by Dunsin Oyekan and “Eze Abata” by Ambassador Chinyere Udoma.

The service brought together members of the entertainment industry, friends, church members and family to celebrate a man whose life touched different generations through his craft, generosity, mentorship and faith.

 

The post ‘Who will comfort my broken heart?’ Francis Duru’s wife breaks down at tribute night appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Fani-Kayode reveals how Gaddafi threatened to trek to Abuja
articles.summary:
Former Minister of Aviation, Femi Fani-Kayode, has recounted how former Libyan leader, Muammar Gaddafi, threatened to trek from the airport to Abuja in 2006 after Nigerian security officials blocked his convoy over weapons found in the vehicles during his visit.

Fani-Kayode, now Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, said the incident occurred on November 26, 2006, when Gaddafi arrived in Nigeria for the African and South American Heads of State Summit.

In an account marking the 20th anniversary of the visit on his X handle yesterday, the former minister said he received Gaddafi on behalf of then President Olusegun Obasanjo and was assigned to accompany the Libyan leader throughout his four-day stay.

He recalled that Gaddafi arrived with about 200 bodyguards, each carrying a sidearm, while at least 100 vehicles had been sent ahead to convey him to Abuja.

According to Fani-Kayode, the boots of the vehicles were loaded with AK-47 rifles and other sophisticated weapons taken from the three aircraft that brought the Libyan leader and his delegation.

He said Nigerian security personnel and military officers stopped the convoy at the airport gate, explaining that although Gaddafi, his delegation and bodyguards could enter with their sidearms, the heavy weapons in the vehicles would not be allowed into the country.

Fani-Kayode said he was in the car with Gaddafi and had to explain the situation to him through an interpreter, adding that the convoy attempted to leave the airport three times but was blocked on each occasion.

Recounting the dramatic moment, he said Gaddafi eventually lost his temper, stepped out of his vehicle and began walking towards Abuja under the scorching sun, with his bodyguards and delegation following him.

“Gaddafi totally lost his temper, got out of his car and started walking under the burning sun, past the airport gate and towards Abuja, saying that if the cars were not allowed in, he would walk there instead. Every single one of his 200 bodyguards and delegation members walked behind him!” he recalled.

Fani-Kayode said he became worried that the Libyan leader could collapse from the heat, as he was already sweating profusely and panting.

He said his appeals to Gaddafi to return to the airport were ignored until he contacted Obasanjo, who told him he was on his way to the airport to catch a flight to Lagos.

According to him, the then President asked him to inform Gaddafi that he was coming to resolve the disagreement personally, after which the Libyan leader agreed to return to the airport.

Fani-Kayode recalled that the two leaders exchanged warm greetings and embraced when Obasanjo arrived, after which the President briefly spoke with Gaddafi before preparing to leave for Lagos.

However, he said Obasanjo privately instructed him that the Libyan delegation must not be allowed to proceed unless the heavy weapons were removed from the vehicles and returned to the aircraft.

“However, as he walked past me, he bent over and whispered into my ear that under no circumstances would Gaddafi and his team be allowed in unless they complied with our request that they drop the AK-47s from the boots of their cars and put them back on their plane,” he said.

The former minister said he subsequently informed Gaddafi that the weapons had to be removed, despite resistance from the Libyan Minister of National Security and Head of Protocol.

He alleged that the two officials were rude to Nigerian security officers, military personnel and Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials, threatening to take Gaddafi back to Libya and boycott the summit if their weapons were not allowed into the country.

Fani-Kayode said the Libyan officials eventually complied, with the weapons removed from the vehicles and loaded back onto the aircraft, while Nigerian soldiers surrounded the plane to ensure they were not taken out again.

The convoy was subsequently allowed to leave the airport for Abuja.

He said his wife, Regina, called during the incident to inform him that the BBC was reporting the disagreement, but he assured her that the matter had been resolved.

Fani-Kayode also recalled that Gaddafi remained silent throughout the journey into Abuja, speaking only when they drove past the National Mosque, which he described as beautiful.

Reflecting on the incident, the former minister said it taught him important lessons about diplomacy, particularly the need for firmness, mutual respect and adherence to established rules.

“It was that day that I learnt about the intricacies of diplomacy and the fact that firmness, the display of mutual respect and a strict adherence to the rules of engagement were vital,” he said.

He praised Nigerian security personnel for standing by their instructions and commended Obasanjo for insisting that the weapons should not be allowed into the country.

Fani-Kayode claimed that the decision was particularly important because, according to information presented at a subsequent Federal Executive Council meeting, Libyan officials had previously taken weapons into Nigeria and handed them to local associates.

He alleged that such weapons later became part of arms stockpiles used by terrorists, insurgents and other non-state actors.

The former minister said Gaddafi’s attitude towards him changed after the airport disagreement was resolved, adding that they became close during the summit and the Libyan leader later invited him to visit Libya as his personal guest.

He said Gaddafi’s only complaint during the four-day engagement was that he wore a suit every day instead of traditional Nigerian attire.

“The only complaint he had was that I had worn a suit for each of those days and that he would have preferred me to wear an agbada or babariga,” he said.

Fani-Kayode also recalled Gaddafi’s death on October 20, 2011, in his hometown of Sirte, Libya, saying he was saddened after watching footage of the former leader’s killing on CNN.

“No one deserves to be killed in such a barbaric manner,” he said.

He said Gaddafi’s violent death, despite his former position of power, demonstrated how quickly political authority could disappear.

“What hit me even more was the fact that the Head of Protocol, who spoke so loudly and aggressively on the day of our encounter and who said that if we did not allow the arms to be taken in, they would fly Gaddafi back home, was one of those condemning him on CNN all the way from Paris on the day he was murdered,” he added.
